title: A week in Atlanta
summary: Seven days of civil rights history, Southern cooking, BeltLine walks and a few places to stay, from Sweet Auburn to the Westside.
author: Nate Bird

places.name: The Georgian Terrace Hotel
places.notes: A 1911 hotel across the street from the Fox Theatre. Ask for a room facing Peachtree.

places.name: Hotel Clermont
places.address: 789 Ponce de Leon Ave NE, Atlanta, GA 30306
places.notes: A restored 1924 hotel with a rooftop bar, a short walk from Ponce City Market and the BeltLine.

places.name: The Candler Hotel Atlanta
places.notes: Asa Candler's 1906 office tower, now a hotel. Handy for the Centennial Park museums.

places.name: The St. Regis Atlanta
places.address: 88 W Paces Ferry Rd NW, Atlanta, GA 30305
places.notes: The splurge. Quiet Buckhead, a big pool, and the Atlanta History Center down the road.

places.name: Mary Mac's Tea Room
places.address: 224 Ponce de Leon Ave NE, Atlanta, GA 30308
places.notes: Southern plates since 1945. Start with the pot likker and cornbread.

places.name: The Varsity
places.notes: Chili dogs, onion rings and a frosted orange, served fast since 1928.

places.name: Busy Bee Cafe
places.address: 810 Martin Luther King Jr Dr SW, Atlanta, GA 30314
places.notes: Fried chicken and sides since 1947. Expect a line at lunch, and it's worth it.

places.name: Paschal's
places.notes: Where civil rights leaders met to plan in the 1960s. Fried chicken and peach cobbler.

places.name: Fox Bros. Bar-B-Q
places.notes: Texas-style brisket and smoked wings. Get the Brunswick stew on the side.

places.name: Antico Pizza Napoletana
places.notes: Wood-fired Neapolitan pizza at shared tables in the middle of the kitchen.

places.name: Krog Street Market
places.notes: A food hall in an old warehouse right on the BeltLine. Good when the group can't agree.

places.name: Ticonderoga Club
places.notes: A small cocktail bar tucked in the back of Krog Street Market, with a short, good food menu.

places.name: Gunshow
places.notes: Kevin Gillespie's chefs bring dishes to your table and you say yes or no. Book ahead.

places.name: Bacchanalia
places.address: 1460 Ellsworth Industrial Blvd NW, Atlanta, GA 30318
places.notes: The special-occasion dinner of the week: a long tasting menu from Anne Quatrano.

places.name: Miller Union
places.notes: Seasonal Southern cooking from Steven Satterfield. The farm egg in celery cream is the one to order.

places.name: Talat Market
places.notes: Thai cooking made with Georgia produce. Loud, fun, and spicy if you ask.

places.name: Sweet Auburn Curb Market
places.notes: A city market since 1918. Lunch from the stalls before the King historic site, five minutes away.

places.name: Lee's Bakery
places.notes: Banh mi on fresh baguettes, cheap and quick. A good first stop on Buford Highway.

places.name: Desta Ethiopian Kitchen
places.notes: Big platters of Ethiopian stews on injera, with a patio that's busy every night.

places.name: Kimball House
places.notes: Oysters and cocktails in Decatur's old train depot. Go for happy hour.

places.name: Bones
places.notes: An old-school steakhouse open since 1979, with white tablecloths and a deep wine list.

places.name: Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park
places.notes: Dr. King's birth home, Ebenezer Baptist Church and his tomb, all on one street. Book the free birth home tour early in the day.

places.name: National Center for Civil and Human Rights
places.address: 100 Ivan Allen Jr Blvd NW, Atlanta, GA 30313
places.notes: The lunch counter simulation is hard to sit through, and that's the point. Allow two hours.

places.name: Georgia Aquarium
places.notes: Whale sharks in one enormous tank. Go at opening to beat the school groups.

places.name: World of Coca-Cola
places.mapsSkip: Apple Maps search returns Coca Cola Pl, not the museum; address checked by hand
places.notes: Corporate, but fun. Finish in the tasting room with drinks from around the world.

places.name: High Museum of Art
places.notes: Richard Meier's white building holds a strong folk and self-taught art collection.

places.name: Fox Theatre
places.notes: A 1929 movie palace with a starry ceiling. See a show, or take the daytime tour.

places.name: Atlanta History Center
places.address: 130 W Paces Ferry Rd NW, Atlanta, GA 30305
places.notes: The Cyclorama, Swan House and 33 acres of gardens. Easily half a day.

places.name: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum
places.address: 441 John Lewis Freedom Pkwy NE, Atlanta, GA 30307
places.notes: A presidency and a long life after it. The Japanese garden out back is a calm stop.

places.name: Ponce City Market
places.address: 675 Ponce de Leon Ave NE, Atlanta, GA 30308
places.notes: A huge old Sears building with a food hall, shops and a rooftop with skyline views and mini golf.

places.name: Historic Oakland Cemetery
places.notes: Victorian gardens and Margaret Mitchell's grave, with the downtown skyline behind. Lovely at golden hour.

places.name: Center for Puppetry Arts
places.notes: Jim Henson's own Muppets, and puppets from around the world. Better for adults than it sounds.

places.name: Fernbank Museum
places.notes: Big dinosaurs inside, and a walk through an old-growth forest outside.

places.name: Delta Flight Museum
places.notes: Walk through a 747 in the old hangars next to the airport. Easy before an evening flight.

places.name: Zoo Atlanta
places.notes: Gorillas and a leafy setting inside Grant Park. Pair it with Oakland Cemetery.

places.name: Buford Highway Farmers Market
places.notes: An international grocery the size of a warehouse. Come hungry and wander the aisles.

places.name: Piedmont Park
places.notes: The city's big lawn, with skyline views over Lake Clara Meer. Pick up a picnic on the way.

places.name: Atlanta Botanical Garden
places.notes: The canopy walk through the treetops, and the orchid house. Check for evening events.

places.name: Atlanta BeltLine Eastside Trail
places.notes: Walk or rent a bike from Piedmont Park to Krog Street, past murals, patios and Ponce City Market.

places.name: Historic Fourth Ward Park
places.notes: A small park built around a stormwater lake, right off the BeltLine.

places.name: Shirley Clarke Franklin Park
places.notes: The city's largest park, opened as Westside Park, around an old quarry turned reservoir. Big views, few crowds.

places.name: Cochran Shoals
places.address: Interstate N Pkwy SE, Atlanta, GA 30339
places.notes: A flat loop along the Chattahoochee River, part of the national recreation area. Good for a morning run.
